title: Rome: some Mass mysteries need silence — so they must not be written for the world
source_text: XXXII. Denique Doctores Ecclesiae Romanae pro traditione non scripta argumentum desumunt a dignitate mysteriorum religionis Christianae. Nam inquiunt, sunt mysteria multa quae silentium requirunt, nec decet ut in Scripturis, quae toti mundo leguntur, explicentur. Si enim ad videnda tremenda mysteria Missae non licet admittere ullos non baptizatos, quomodo licebit eis eadem scripto tradere?
pass_a_gloss: Finally the Doctors of the Roman Church take an argument for unwritten tradition from the dignity of the mysteries of the Christian religion. For they say, there are many mysteries which require silence, and it is not fitting that they be explained in the Scriptures, which are read by the whole world. For if to see the tremendous mysteries of the Mass it is not permitted to admit any who are not baptized, how will it be permitted to hand the same things over to them in writing?
pass_b_english: Last dignity argument: some mysteries demand silence.
Scripture is read by the whole world — so Rome says those secrets must stay out of it.
Unbaptized may not watch the tremendous Mass mysteries.
Therefore, they ask, how may the same things be delivered to them in writing?
